summary: On November 19, the International Court of Justice delivered a historic ruling: finding Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. Malaysia has long been a supporter of the persecuted Muslim minority. But its role as a safe haven is coming to an end, amid a rise in hate speech and calls for the expulsion of Rohingya via social media.

summary: The world watched with bated breath Thursday as the presidents of China, Russia and the United States met for 90 minutes for an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen. summary: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Olivia Cheung. summary: Mexico's military forces captured ​one of the most wanted suspected drug lords, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," the military announced on Saturday, after a deadly firefight that killed seven suspected attackers and four soldiers. summary: US President Donald Trump played up his "fantastic" relationships with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin during a White House press conference on Friday following his return to Washington after a first-ever trilateral meeting with the Chinese and Russian leaders. title: Jamaica's beaches are increasingly off limits to locals
summary: Jamaica usually conjures up images of white sandy beaches, Rastafari culture and Bob Marley – but another reality exists. On this small Caribbean island, less than 1 percent of the coastline is freely accessible to local people. The rest has gradually been privatised, mostly for large hotel developments and private homes.

title: El Salvador: Nayib Bukele, self-proclaimed “coolest dictator on earth”, is seeking a third term
summary: 🇸🇻 El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele, who calls himself the “coolest dictator on earth”, is seeking a third term after changing the Constitution to scrap presidential term limits. His war on gangs has made him hugely popular, but also sparked serious human rights concerns.

title: White House fires national cyber director over widespread outages
summary: The White House fired national cyber director Sean Cairncross on Thursday following a week of technology disruptions affecting US air travel, email services and national security systems. The departure comes as the Trump administration faces criticism over its response to the outages, which officials say were unrelated incidents.

title: Armed forces in Haiti kill at least 34 gang members to regain control of key corridor
summary: Haitian security forces launched a major offensive on Thursday to retake Martissant, a strategic corridor linking Port-au-Prince with the country's western and southern regions that gangs have controlled for five years. Police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in clashes involving a private security task force.

title: A president among body bags: Photo ops spark outrage in Colombia
summary: Since taking office in August, Colombia's far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella has regularly posted videos that show him walking among body bags supposedly holding the remains of rebel fighters – a communications strategy that has sparked widespread criticism.

title: NASA's Voyager 1 phones home from record one light-day away, 49 years after launch
summary: The Voyager 1 probe launched by NASA nearly a half century ago has reached a distance from Earth of one light day (more than 26 billion kilometres), the farthest any human artifact has ever ventured from our planet. The space agency received a signal from the spacecraft Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent.

title: US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black speaker of the House
summary: Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday to be the next speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on track to make history as the nation’s first Black American with the gavel.

title: Peltola defeats Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, expanding Democratic majority
summary: Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska on Tuesday, completing a political comeback in a state that US President Donald Trump has repeatedly won by wide margins. Her victory gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority, marking their biggest net gain in Senate seats since 1958.

title: Haitians rally behind Bukele as Salvadoran troops battle gangs
summary: Thousands of Haitians took to the streets on Tuesday to urge El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele to keep fighting gangs, as his troops bolster security forces in the Caribbean nation. But experts warn that growing public support could turn to anger without a long-term plan to tackle violence and strengthen Haiti's police.

title: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles-free status as deaths mount
summary: The US has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus has spread at the fastest rate in more than 30 years, while Mexico and Bolivia also lost their measles-elimination status. Vaccination rates have been falling against a number of diseases, in the US and globally, and measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024.

title: Iran 'playing mind games with the United States', expert says
summary: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Monte Francis, Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center in Washington, says that Iran may be "playing mind games with the United States as a way perhaps of deterring President Trump from unleashing a massive new attack on Iran".

summary: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
summary: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. title: Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
summary: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial site on Saturday evening, as two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran reported shooting down a US drone amid stalled efforts to end the war.

title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for coalition talks, his centrist Yashar party said Saturday. The "marathon series of talks" starts Sunday, the party said, adding that the move reflected a commitment to form "the broadest possible government" after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.

title: Iraqi security forces deploy in Hezbollah stronghold under compromise deal
summary: Iraqi security forces deployed ​in the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar, state media said on Friday, under a compromise deal brokered by Shi'ite politicians. Iraq's prime minister ordered a security intervention earlier this week after accusing the Iran-backed militia of smuggling state-owned oil worth ⁠hundreds of millions of dollars.

title: Gazans flee shelters as Israeli army launches ground operation beyond Yellow Line
summary: Palestinians fled their tents and shelters in central Gaza on Wednesday after Israel launched a rare ground operation in an area it withdrew ​from under a ‌2025 ceasefire. The Israeli army said it crossed the Yellow Line separating Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas "to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip".

title: Yemen: Why the Houthis may besiege Aden rather than storm it
summary: Bolstered by their recent military successes, Houthi rebels this week advanced close to the southern port city of Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised Yemeni government. Amid territorial ambitions, regional rivalries, and divisions within government forces, the potential fall of this stronghold could permanently alter the balance of power in the country.

title: Loud blast rocks Riyadh as Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missiles
summary: A powerful explosion rattled homes in Riyadh on Wednesday, journalists and residents said, as the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said they intercepted two cruise missiles fired by the Iran-backed militia. In Gaza, the Israeli military launched a rare ground operation in a Hamas-controlled area, leading dozens of families to flee their tents and shelters. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

title: Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as speaker in blow for Netanyahu
summary: The Israeli parliament on Tuesday elected as new speaker an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace current Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Matan Kahana, a former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of the agenda of Netanyahu.

title: Major setbacks for Netanyahu ahead of vote to name new Knesset speaker
summary: Since suffering heavy losses in Israel’s Oct. 27 election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party has repeatedly claimed the vote was “stolen” by Arab-led parties, possibly with foreign assistance. Those claims appear to be crumbling as he tries to cling to power, as the Israeli parliament is set to select a new speaker opposed to him. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

title: Breaking taboos: Egypt's sexual revolution takes to social media
summary: In Egypt, a sexual revolution is quietly unfolding on social media. Accounts followed by tens of thousands of people, with posts attracting millions of views, are tackling a wide range of issues surrounding sexuality – from the widespread practice of female genital mutilation (which 93 per cent of women in rural areas have undergone) to sex education and sexual pleasure.

title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu ‘cannot remain’ after alleged election interference by aide
summary: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately following reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. The former army chief called Netanyahu and his entourage an "immediate threat to democracy", hours after representatives discussed forming a national unity government.
